body.statement: Fix \(N\), \(K\), and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\), and restrict the input to a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either with its exact entries or by a rational law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) inducing those entries. Characterize the cone \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this feasible domain and hence the label-free set \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): equivalently, decide whether some common unit relabelling \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and every \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length that returns such a relabelling and a finite cut certificate on yes instances, and returns arm-specific binary ordered columns together with \(\sigma\) giving a strict exact loss improvement on no instances; if binary separation is not complete, characterize the minimal finite alphabet required for a complete separating certificate.
body.justification: The feasible moment-polytope domain separates genuine randomization kernels from arbitrary four-index arrays and turns universal rank preservation into a label-invariant decision problem.
body.gap: Brennan et al. solve feasible design instances numerically, while Laurent and Seminaroti give a sufficient Robinson--Toeplitz identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem rather than a necessary-and-sufficient certificate over balanced assignment-law covariance tensors.
body.consumer: Designers of matched, paired, rerandomized, and geographically balanced experiments receive a certificate tied to a realizable assignment law, or an exact finite completion showing why rank-preserving imputation fails.
